newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU Parliament backs 1997/98 farm price freeze.
newsitem.headline: EU Parliament backs 1997/98 farm price freeze.

text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday voted broadly in favour of proposals for a virtual freeze in farm prices in 1997/98 with spending set at 41 billion ecus.
The European Commission proposed in March mostly unchanged farm prices in 1997/98 (July/June), apart from some small changes to cereals, rice, sugar, flax and hemp payments.

But the Parliament backed a report by British Euro MP Robert Sturdy criticising a Commission proposal to cut the monthly increment for storing cereals. It called for payments to be kept at current levels.
On sugar, the Parliament called for a slight increase in storage aid to take account of what it said was a long overdue review of storage costs. The Commission has called for a cut.
The Parliament only has an advisory role in fixing the annual farm price package which is due to be finalised by EU farm ministers at a meeting in Luxembourg from June 23-25.
